description: Buddy arrives in Ladner under a stolen clerical identity and discovers that fooling a congregation requires constant improvisation while people from his previous life remain inconveniently alive.

s01e01.description: Fleeing gambling debts and criminal trouble, Buddy steals a pastor’s identity and convinces a small-town Lutheran congregation that he is their newly appointed minister.

s01e02.description: Buddy secretly returns home for his own funeral, only to come back to Ladner and discover two deaths have made the new pastor a police suspect.

s01e03.description: Buddy’s first sermon alarms Schmidt enough to summon the bishop for an evaluation, while Dora makes an unusual request and Alexa and Russell compete for Buddy’s attention.

s01e04.description: Another gambling loss drives Buddy to steal a ruby necklace from a corpse, while Dora and Alexa clash over a church fashion show and Schmidt becomes infatuated with a stranger.

s01e05.description: Buddy tries to help Alexa escape people from her dangerous past and puts them both at risk, while Dora struggles after learning her former fiancé is getting married.

s01e06.description: Buddy reveals a personal truth about Russell to Russell’s parents and receives a major surprise in return, complicating the false pastor’s already precarious private life.

s01e07.description: Kenny’s body is discovered, forcing Buddy to answer questions from Alexa, Schmidt and the police while a young blackmailer obtains compromising evidence against him.

s01e08.description: A newly arrived family threatens Buddy’s position in Ladner, Dora asks for help with a strange compulsion, and Schmidt continues his secret relationship with Ashlee.

s01e09.description: An unexpected delivery risks exposing Buddy’s real identity just as a hired killer arrives in Ladner, while Schmidt’s wife begins suspecting him of an affair.

s01e10.description: With an assassin hunting him and his false identity increasingly unsafe, Buddy concludes that staying in Ladner may finally be more dangerous than running again.
